testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual brake system, a driver should:

options.text: Let the engine warm up so fuel reaches the engine.
Wait for air pressure to build in both the primary and secondary systems.
Start driving right after the engine starts.
Pump the pedal 20 times to build pressure, then start driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for air pressure to build in both the primary and secondary systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, wait for the compressor to build pressure to at least 100 psi in both systems.

questions.question: If your tractor has ABS but your trailer does not, the ABS:

options.text: Will still improve your steering control.
Will make your brake lights brighter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will still improve your steering control.
questions.explanation: If your tractor has ABS but your trailer does not, the ABS will still improve steering control. Watch your trailer and ease off the brakes if it starts to swing.

questions.question: Test the low pressure warning signal by:

options.text: Turning on the engine and applying the trailer hand brake.
Quickly pressing and releasing the brake pedal.
Removing wheel blocks and releasing the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Quickly pressing and releasing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: After the system charges, test the warning signal by quickly pressing and releasing the brake pedal. This releases air from the system. The warning signal should turn on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: To use the stab braking method, you should:

options.text: Apply full brakes until wheels lock, release until wheels roll again, then repeat.
Apply brakes halfway while keeping wheels rolling.
Apply full brakes until wheels lock and the vehicle stops.
Apply the emergency brake until the vehicle slows.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply full brakes until wheels lock, release until wheels roll again, then repeat.
questions.explanation: Stab braking for emergency stops means fully applying brakes until they lock. Then release the brakes until the wheels start rolling. Repeat this process.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). Other air brake vehicles made on or after March 1, 1998 must also have ABS.

questions.question: The air compressor governor controls:

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks.
The temperature of air in the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: When an S-cam turns inside a brake drum, it:

options.text: Pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the drum.
Pushes the brake shoes against the brake linings.
Pushes the brake linings against the wheel axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the drum.
questions.explanation: When the brake pedal is pressed, the S-cam turns and pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: The application pressure gauge shows:

options.text: How much air pressure is being used for braking.
The temperature of air in the brake system.
The pressure of air from the compressor.
How many times the brakes have been used.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being used for braking.
questions.explanation: The application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is applied to the brakes. Not all air brake systems have this gauge.

questions.question: Emergency brakes:
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. These brakes must be held by mechanical force.

questions.question: Air brakes use ____ to work.
questions.explanation: Air brakes work by using compressed air.

questions.question: A ____ lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes.
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes. The driver controls it with a lever on the dashboard.

questions.question: When you push the brake pedal, air brakes work:

options.text: Only if the green lever on the control panel is pushed down.

questions.explanation: When you push the brake pedal in a vehicle with air brakes, air takes half a second or more to flow through the lines and make the brakes work. Hydraulic brakes in cars and light trucks work instantly when the pedal is pushed.

questions.question: Where must the ABS malfunction lamp be located on a dolly with ABS?
questions.explanation: A dolly with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) must have a yellow malfunction lamp on its left side.

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The time it takes for brakes to work after the brake pedal is pushed
The distance between the brake pedal's resting position and the floor
The amount of air pressure needed to stop a vehicle
How worn out the brakes are

questions.correctAnswerText: The time it takes for brakes to work after the brake pedal is pushed
questions.explanation: Air brakes have a delay because air needs time to flow through the lines. Brake lag is at least half a second between when you push the pedal and when the brakes start to work. Hydraulic brakes work instantly.

questions.question: While going downhill, brake until you reach a speed that is ____ below your safe speed, then release the pedal.
questions.explanation: While going downhill, hold the brake pedal until your vehicle drops to 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the pedal. Repeat as needed.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, the driver should:

options.text: Pull out the air brake knob.

questions.explanation: To stop a vehicle with air brakes during normal driving, press the brake pedal down.

questions.question: Brakes can go out of adjustment:

options.text: If they are used at all.
If one side's brakes are used more than the other side.

questions.explanation: Hot brakes are most likely to go out of adjustment. Use proper braking methods to keep your brakes from overheating.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use:
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems. These are two separate braking systems that work with one set of controls. Each system operates the brakes on different axles.

questions.question: Once the air tanks reach 125 psi, the air compressor governor will:

options.text: Stop the compressor from pumping air.
Begin pumping air into the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping air once the tanks reach about 125 psi. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended:

options.text: Use the parking brake only if the vehicle is on a slope.
Do not use the parking brake because it can damage the tires.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when parked. However, do not use it if your brakes are very hot or if they are wet and it is freezing.

questions.question: What is a dual air brake system?

options.text: One air brake system with two sets of controls.
One air brake system for each side of the truck.
Two separate air brake systems controlled by one set of controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two separate air brake systems controlled by one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems that work with one set of controls. One system controls the rear axle brakes. The other system controls the front axle brakes.

questions.question: When should you use the parking brake?

options.text: Every time you park the vehicle.
To stop the vehicle during normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park your vehicle.

questions.question: Is a low air pressure warning signal required on vehicles with air brakes?
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal. If this signal goes off while driving, stop the vehicle right away and have the system checked.

questions.question: How long should it take for air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi in a dual air brake system?
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, the air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in both systems in about 45 seconds.

questions.question: What should you do when traveling down a steep downgrade?

options.text: Shift into a lower gear, then use brakes to help slow the engine.
Keep downshifting instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into a lower gear, then use brakes to help slow the engine.
questions.explanation: On a downgrade, use the engine's braking power as your main way to control speed. Shift to a lower gear before going down the hill. Use the brakes only when you need extra slowing or stopping.
